root_idea.summary: A root oriented toward severity, constriction, and entanglement in an affair.
root_idea.development: Its lexical development extends from compact or muscular flesh and physical constriction to obstructed marriage, difficult or unmanageable affairs, severe disease, crowded or choked spaces, and impeded childbirth.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form عَضَلَ.

senses.definition: To wrongfully obstruct, withhold, or constrain a woman in a marital matter—especially by preventing her from marrying or remarrying.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in Quranic legal contexts for severe obstruction: preventing divorced women from marrying their husbands, and constraining women in a way intended to pressure them regarding what they were given. The varying renderings “hinder” and “constrain” reflect the same obstruction construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strike or hit someone’s muscle.
Straitening; prevention, withholding, or debarring.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The general verbal noun and primary semantic branch of constriction or obstruction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be muscular, brawny, or richly supplied with muscle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a man, especially one large in the muscle of the shank.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Muscular, musculous, or brawny.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a man having many muscles or prominent musculature, especially in the shank.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Compact in flesh and unseemly or lacking beauty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An epithet applied to a woman.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make an affair or situation strait, obstructing the way to what is desired.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with عَلَيْهِ and related constructions; also said of a thing becoming strait, and figuratively of land or a place becoming choked or crowded with people.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have an offspring or egg become stuck so that birth or laying is difficult.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a woman, ewe, goat, hen, bird, and similar creatures in the reported obstetric or laying construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become fatigued from travel, riding, or work.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a she-camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become hard, difficult, or apparently closed to someone; to exhaust or overcome him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of an affair or case, and of a severe disease that defeats or wearies physicians.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have many branches and become tangled, luxuriant, or dense.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported Q.Q. Form IV usage said of a tree; the associated participial form is textually disputed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Very cunning or highly intelligent, with craft and foresight.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a man.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bad, evil, foul, or unseemly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a thing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A large rat, or specifically the male of a rat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Its plural is reported as عِضْلَانٌ; the vocalization is discussed in the lexical evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Muscular, musculous, or brawny.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a man having many muscles or a large shank muscle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A calamity or great misfortune.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression عُضْلَةٌ مِنَ العُضَلِ, “a calamity among calamities.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: A muscle: a mass of firm flesh attached to a tendon or sinew.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Especially a muscle of the shank; the regular plural is عَضَلَاتٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A reported name for a tree resembling the oleander.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A disputed attribution: one authority reports this sense, while another judges the word to be a form of عَصَلَةٌ instead.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Severe, distressing, or difficult to remedy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Of a disease, one that resists cure and exhausts physicians; of an affair, one hard to undertake or manage; and of an oath, one severe or onerous.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Base, ignoble, or mean; narrow or illiberal in disposition.
A hard, strait, or difficult affair for which no way of carrying it out can be found.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to an affair or case.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A difficult or distressing event, calamity, affair, case, or question.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Especially a matter whose means of resolution or escape are difficult to find.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Firm, strong, or compact in build.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A physical description derived from the muscle sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having offspring or an egg stuck so that it cannot come forth easily.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An epithet applied to a woman, sheep, goat, hen, or similar creature in the reported childbirth or laying construction.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Covers marital obstruction and the stated broader branch of straitening or prevention.
Distinct action of striking a muscle.
Form I state of being muscular.
Making an affair strait and obstructing the desired outcome.
Intransitive straitening is covered by the same Form II branch.
Figurative crowding and choking are included in the Form II straitening branch.
Fatigue of a she-camel from travel, riding, or work.
An affair becoming hard, closed, or difficult.
The associated sense of an affair exhausting or overcoming a person.
Reported Q.Q. usage for a dense or tangled tree.
Muscle or compact flesh on a tendon.
Participial form for impeded childbirth or laying.
Pointer to an entry under another lexical headword.

cautions: The reported tree sense of عَضَلَةٌ is retained as disputed evidence because the lexical source attributes it to one authority but another identifies it as a likely form of عَصَلَةٌ instead.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: The tree sense under عَضَلَةٌ is materially lexical but disputed within the source tradition; it is represented only with that qualification.
